digitalocean_droplet: `digitalocean_droplet` looks up a real, already-created Droplet -- DigitalOcean's own virtual machine, with its real current size, image, region, and networking.
digitalocean_endpoint: `digitalocean_endpoint` looks up a real, already-created CDN endpoint -- the fully qualified domain name DigitalOcean's own edge network serves cached content from, backed by a Space or a custom origin.
digitalocean_event: `digitalocean_event` looks up a real, already-recorded App Platform event -- one entry in an application's own real activity log (a deployment starting, a build failing, a job completing).
digitalocean_firewall: `digitalocean_firewall` looks up a real, already-created cloud firewall -- the inbound/outbound rule set DigitalOcean enforces at the network edge for whichever Droplets or tags it's applied to.
digitalocean_floating_ip: `digitalocean_floating_ip` looks up a real, already-reserved floating IP -- a publicly routable IPv4 address that can be reassigned between Droplets in a region without any DNS propagation delay.
digitalocean_image: `digitalocean_image` looks up a real, already-available image -- a Droplet base OS, a DigitalOcean-provided one-click application, or a custom snapshot/backup image usable to create new Droplets.
digitalocean_key: `digitalocean_key` looks up a real, already-registered SSH key -- the public key material DigitalOcean can embed into a Droplet's own `authorized_keys` file at creation time.
digitalocean_load_balancer: `digitalocean_load_balancer` looks up a real, already-created Load Balancer -- the forwarding rules, health checks, and backend Droplet set it distributes traffic across.
digitalocean_namespace: `digitalocean_namespace` looks up a real, already-created Functions namespace -- the deployment boundary a set of related serverless functions is grouped and versioned under.
digitalocean_nfs_get_response: `digitalocean_nfs_get_response` looks up a real, already-provisioned NFS share -- a network file-storage volume, its performance tier, size, and the VPCs allowed to mount it.
digitalocean_node_pool: `digitalocean_node_pool` looks up a real, already-created node pool inside a DigitalOcean Kubernetes cluster -- the group of worker nodes sharing one machine size and autoscaling configuration that actually runs cluster workloads.
digitalocean_pool: `digitalocean_pool` looks up a real, already-created PgBouncer connection pool for a managed PostgreSQL cluster -- the pooling mode and size that let many client connections share a smaller number of real backend connections.
digitalocean_project: `digitalocean_project` looks up a real, already-created project -- the grouping DigitalOcean uses to organize a set of resources (Droplets, volumes, domains, and more) together for billing and organizational visibility, independent of what type each resource is.
digitalocean_record: `digitalocean_record` looks up a real, already-created DNS record inside a domain's own zone -- one A, CNAME, MX, TXT, or other record DigitalOcean's name servers actually serve.
digitalocean_registry: `digitalocean_registry` looks up a real, already-created container registry -- the account-wide, globally unique image store and its subscription tier, distinct from the individual repositories and tags stored inside it.
digitalocean_replica: `digitalocean_replica` looks up a real, already-created read-only replica of a managed database cluster -- a separate connection endpoint serving read traffic without adding load to the primary.
digitalocean_reserved_ip: `digitalocean_reserved_ip` looks up a real, already-reserved IPv4 address (DigitalOcean's own current name for what was previously called a floating IP) -- a publicly routable address reassignable between Droplets in a region.
digitalocean_reserved_ipv6: `digitalocean_reserved_ipv6` looks up a real, already-reserved IPv6 address -- the IPv6 counterpart to a reserved IP, tied to a specific region rather than a specific Droplet.
digitalocean_saa: `digitalocean_saa` looks up a real, already-enabled Add-on for a resource -- the association between an account's own resource and one of DigitalOcean's optional add-on services (such as Scheduled Snapshot Protection).
digitalocean_scan: `digitalocean_scan` looks up a real, already-run security scan -- the result of DigitalOcean's own scanning service checking a resource for known vulnerabilities.
digitalocean_sink: `digitalocean_sink` looks up a real, already-configured metrics or log sink for a managed database cluster -- one of possibly several forwarding destinations for that cluster's own operational data.
digitalocean_snapshot: `digitalocean_snapshot` looks up a real, already-created snapshot -- a point-in-time image of a Droplet or a block storage volume, usable to create a new Droplet or volume from that exact saved state.
digitalocean_tag: `digitalocean_tag` looks up a real, already-created tag -- the label attachable to Droplets, images, volumes, snapshots, and database clusters, along with the real, current count of resources it's applied to.
digitalocean_topic: `digitalocean_topic` looks up a real, already-created Kafka topic inside a managed database cluster.
digitalocean_trigger: `digitalocean_trigger` looks up a real, already-configured Functions trigger -- the schedule or event source that invokes a specific function inside a namespace without a direct HTTP call.
digitalocean_user: `digitalocean_user` looks up a real, already-created database user inside a managed database cluster -- the credential a client authenticates with, distinct from the cluster's own default admin user.
digitalocean_vectordb_get_vector_dbrespo: `digitalocean_vectordb_get_vector_dbresponse` looks up a real, already-provisioned Gradient AI Platform vector database -- the managed store used for embedding-based retrieval, sized and regioned independently of any one knowledge base or agent.
digitalocean_volume: `digitalocean_volume` looks up a real, already-created Block Storage volume -- an independently resizable SSD volume attachable to a Droplet, outliving the Droplet's own lifecycle.
digitalocean_vpc: `digitalocean_vpc` looks up a real, already-created VPC -- the private, isolated network a region's own Droplets and other resources can be placed inside, with no public routing by default.
digitalocean_vpc_nat_gateway: `digitalocean_vpc_nat_gateway` looks up a real, already-created VPC NAT gateway -- the managed egress point that lets resources inside a VPC reach the public internet through one shared, defined address without each needing a public IP of its own.
digitalocean_vpc_peering: `digitalocean_vpc_peering` looks up a real, already-created VPC peering connection -- a private link routing traffic directly between two VPCs without traversing the public internet.
